'''James Michael Lattimer''' (born April 12, 1950, in [[Marion (Indiana)|Marion]], [[Indiana]])<ref>''American Men and Women of Science'', Thomson Gale 2004</ref> is an American nuclear astrophysicist who works on the equation of state for dense [[nuclear matter]] and [[neutron stars]]. He is currently a distinguished professor at [[Stony Brook University]].

==Career==

Lattimer completed his BSc in 1972 at the [[University of Notre Dame]] and his PhD in 1976 at the [[University of Texas at Austin]]. After postdoc positions at the [[University of Chicago]] and [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]], he became a professor at [[Stony Brook University]] in 1979 and a Distinguished Professor of Physics and Astronomy in 2013.<ref>[http://www.astro.sunysb.edu/astro/people.html Stony Brook Astronomy webpage]</ref>

He is also associate editor of the ''[[Physical Review Letters]]''.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/staff |title = PRL Journal Staff|date = 2007-12-03}}</ref>

==Research==
Lattimer has made several fundamental contributions to the field of [[nuclear astrophysics]], with a particular focus on neutron stars. One of his biggest impacts was modeling the birth of neutron stars from
supernovae in 1986 with then-research assistant professor [[Adam Burrows]].<ref>[http://adsabs.harvard.edu/cgi-bin/nph-abs_connect?db_key=AST&db_key=PHY&db_key=PRE&qform=AST&arxiv_sel=astro-ph&arxiv_sel=cond-mat&arxiv_sel=cs&arxiv_sel=gr-qc&arxiv_sel=hep-ex&arxiv_sel=hep-lat&arxiv_sel=hep-ph&arxiv_sel=hep-th&arxiv_sel=math&arxiv_sel=math-ph&arxiv_sel=nlin&arxiv_sel=nucl-ex&arxiv_sel=nucl-th&arxiv_sel=physics&arxiv_sel=quant-ph&arxiv_sel=q-bio&sim_query=YES&ned_query=YES&adsobj_query=YES&aut_logic=OR&obj_logic=OR&author=lattimer%2C+j&object=&start_mon=&start_year=&end_mon=&end_year=&ttl_logic=OR&title=&txt_logic=OR&text=&nr_to_return=2000&start_nr=1&jou_pick=ALL&ref_stems=&data_and=ALL&group_and=ALL&start_entry_day=&start_entry_mon=&start_entry_year=&end_entry_day=&end_entry_mon=&end_entry_year=&min_score=&sort=CITATIONS&data_type=SHORT&aut_syn=YES&ttl_syn=YES&txt_syn=YES&aut_wt=1.0&obj_wt=1.0&ttl_wt=0.3&txt_wt=3.0&aut_wgt=YES&obj_wgt=YES&ttl_wgt=YES&txt_wgt=YES&ttl_sco=YES&txt_sco=YES&version=1 based on citations] from the [[Astrophysics Data System]]</ref> This came just six months

In work that led to his PhD thesis, Lattimer and his advisor [[David Schramm (astrophysicist)|David Schramm]] first argued that the mergers of neutron stars and [[black holes]] would result in the ejection of neutron-rich matter in sufficient quantities to explain the origin of [[r-process]] elements such as gold and platinum.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lattimer |first1=J. M. |last2=Schramm |first2=D. N. |year=1974 |title=Black-hole-neutron-star collisions |journal=The Astrophysical Journal |publisher=IOP Publishing |volume=192 |page=L145 |bibcode=1974ApJ...192L.145L |doi=10.1086/181612 |issn=0004-637X |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lattimer |first1=J. M. |last2=Schramm |first2=D. N. |year=1976 |title=The tidal disruption of neutron stars by black holes in close binaries |journal=The Astrophysical Journal |publisher=IOP Publishing |volume=210 |page=549 |bibcode=1976ApJ...210..549L |doi=10.1086/154860 |issn=0004-637X |doi-access=free |hdl-access=free |hdl=2152/35059}}</ref>  Later, with collaborators, he demonstrated decompressing neutron-star matter from both neutron star-black holes and neutron star-neutron star mergers would form a natural r-process that would match observed patterns.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lattimer |first1=J. G. | title=Direct Observation of the Cooling of the Cassiopeia a Neutron Star | journal=The Astrophysical Journal | publisher=IOP Publishing | volume=719 | issue=2 | date=2010-08-02 | issn=2041-8205 | doi=10.1088/2041-8205/719/2/l167 |doi-access=free| pages=L167–L171| arxiv=1007.4719 |bibcode=2010ApJ...719L.167H}}</ref> rapid cooling of the neutron star in the [[Cassiopeia A]] [[supernova remnant]] is the first direct evidence for [[superfluidity]] and [[superconductivity]] in neutron star interiors.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasa.gov/mission_pages/chandra/news/casa2011.html |title=NASA Press Release |access-date=2014-10-22 |archive-date=2016-01-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160115044412/http://www.nasa.gov/mission_pages/chandra/news/casa2011.html }}</ref> He has collaborated extensively with [[Madappa Prakash]].

==Awards and honors==
In 2015, Lattimer was awarded the [[Hans Bethe Prize]] for "outstanding theoretical work connecting observations of [[supernovae]] and neutron stars with neutrino emission and the equation of state of matter beyond nuclear density."<ref>[http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Lattimer&first_nm=James&year=2015 APS Hans A. Bethe Prize]</ref>

In 1985, he was awarded the Fullam (Ernest F.) Award from [[Dudley Observatory]] (1985).

Lattimer has been elected to the following fellowships:<ref>{{Cite web |title=Awards by Award {{!}} Department of Physics and Astronomy |url=https://www.stonybrook.edu/commcms/physics/about/awards_and_prizes/awards.php |access-date=2024-01-14 |website=www.stonybrook.edu |language=en}}</ref>

* Fellow of American Astronomical Society (2023)
* Fellow of American Physical Society (2001)
* Guggenheim (J.S.) Fellowship (1999)
* Sloan (Alfred P.) Fellowship (1982)
